reply.answer: The widest gap between forward commitments and current liquidity/operating cash flow is at Alphabet and Amazon, which each disclose roughly $900 billion+ in leases-not-started/purchase commitments against operating cash flow of ~$170-180 billion and cash+securities of under $270 billion—commitments are roughly 4-5x annual operating cash flow. Meta (~$455 billion purchase commitments, ~$356 billion unstarted leases vs ~$133 billion operating cash flow) and Oracle ($664 billion backlog, $288 billion unstarted leases vs only $47 billion operating cash flow and $36 billion cash) show even steeper ratios, with Oracle's backlog-to-OCF ratio exceeding 14x. Microsoft's $364.6 billion in not-yet-commenced leases against $196 billion OCF is large in absolute terms but less stretched relatively. Among the smaller AI infrastructure/crypto-miner names (CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, TeraWulf, Core Scientific), backlog and lease commitments (e.g., CoreWeave's $103.7 billion RPO vs $6.9 billion OCF and $35.6 billion debt) represent extreme multiples of current cash generation, making them the most stretched relative to balance-sheet capacity even though absolute dollar amounts are far smaller than the hyperscalers. Oracle stands out as having the largest commitment-to-cash-flow gap among large, rated issuers given its comparatively thin cash and operating cash flow relative to its $664 billion backlog and $288 billion in unstarted leases.
reply.next_question: How much of the contracted backlog (remaining performance obligations) at Oracle, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and CoreWeave depends on a handful of AI customers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic), since such concentration would make the above commitment-to-cash-flow gaps far riskier if any single counterparty's spending slows?
